question.text: How many Swiss regions will be classified as "Extremely Dry" according to the Swiss drought platform on December 1, 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves as the number of Swiss drought regions classified as "Extremely dry" according to the Swiss [National drought platform](https://www.trockenheit.admin.ch/en) when accessed by Metaculus on or after December 1, 2026.

research:
I couldn't find the current number of "Extremely dry" regions. The platform's map doesn't show per-region values in the page text, and no recent article gives a count. The latest counts I found are from June and August. The platform has 38 drought regions on a five-level scale (Not dry, Slightly dry, Dry, Very dry, Extremely dry).

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-02: The national drought platform was last updated on 11/02/2026, covering the situation until 11/01/2026. Its headline says the drought continues: recent rain eased it temporarily in some regions, but the overall situation "remains tense." I could not get the list of levels by region, even with the list view. [trockenheit.admin.ch](https://www.trockenheit.admin.ch/en)
- 2026-10-26: An earlier update (situation to 10/25) carried the same message, according to a search snippet. [trockenheit.admin.ch/fr](https://www.trockenheit.admin.ch/fr)
- 2026-10-29: The weekly bulletin said:
  - The worst deficits are in the central and eastern Alps (Uri and Glarus Alps, Surselva, northern Graubünden), at 50-70%.
  - Soil moisture deficit is "considerable to extreme" on the northern Alpine side and in the Mittelland.
  - The West and Northwest had a locally positive 30-day rain balance, with only a slight 90-day deficit.
  - The next bulletin is due 2026-11-05. [Bulletin](https://www.trockenheit.admin.ch/de/trockenheit/trockenheitsbulletin), [hydrodaten](https://www.hydrodaten.admin.ch/de/bulletin)
- 2026-11-04: A separate swisstopo briefing, by canton rather than by drought region and with its scale undefined, puts 20 cantons at level 4, five (BL, BS, GE, JU, NE) at level 2 and Ticino at level 1. It is probably a hazard-warning scale, not the drought index used for resolution. [swisstopo briefing](https://swisstopo.github.io/topo-drought-briefing/)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. Drought is still widespread, but rain in October eased it in the West, Northwest and Jura, and possibly in Ticino. Those regions have probably dropped below "Extremely dry." This is my inference from the bulletin, not a confirmed reading.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-04: MeteoSwiss forecast a dry day across Switzerland. [TdG](https://www.tdg.ch/meteo-soleil-en-valais-grisaille-sur-le-plateau-ce-mercredi-197978571446)
- 2026-11-02: Graubünden relocated about 5,000 fish. Water levels in most river basins hit historic lows this summer. [swissinfo](https://www.swissinfo.ch/eng/emissions-reduction/gr-around-5000-fish-have-been-relocated-due-to-the-drought/92314947)
- Late October 2026: October rainfall was 44-155% of normal. The Jura up to Basel was wetter than normal. Northern and central Graubünden, Valais, the southern Alps and the Engadin had large deficits. [headtopics/Klimabulletin](https://ch.headtopics.com/news/oktober-war-zu-warm-und-zu-trocken-89459024)
- 2026-10-16: MeteoNews said October was clearly less dry than September. A cold front brought more than 50 mm in places along the Prealps. Drought eased at the surface, but lakes and groundwater stayed near record lows. [MeteoNews](https://meteonews.ch/de/News/N16901/Oktober-deutlich-zu-mild_-etwas-zu-trocken-und-leicht-zu-bew%C3%B6lkt)
- 2026-10-01: SRF said every region was clearly too dry over hydrological year 2025/26. Ending the drought would take several months of above-average rain. [SRF](https://www.srf.ch/meteo/meteo-stories/ende-des-hydrologischen-jahres-wasser-ist-mangelware)
- 2026-09-25: Blick said "nearly all of Switzerland" was at the highest drought level. [Blick](https://www.blick.ch/schweiz/regen-defizit-verschaerft-sich-schweizer-fluesse-fuehren-teils-so-wenig-wasser-wie-kaum-jemals-id22278478.html)

## 4. Base rates and past counts (of 38 regions)
- 2026-06-23: 13 regions were extremely dry, and only the Upper Engadine was not dry. [watson](https://www.watson.ch/schweiz/klima/128161167-wetter-in-der-schweiz-die-hitzewelle-sorgt-fuer-massive-trockenheit)
- About 2026-08-02: 20 extremely dry, 13 very dry, 2 dry, 3 slightly dry. Blick said "more than half" were extremely dry on Aug 2. [Blick](https://www.blick.ch/sonntagsblick/wegen-anhaltender-trockenheit-geht-uns-das-trinkwasser-aus-id22151220.html)
- Late September 2026: no exact count, but "nearly all" regions were at the top level, which suggests well above 20.
- Trend: the count probably peaked in September and is likely lower after the October rain. I found no count for October or November.
- Comparable history is very limited because the platform only launched in 2025. Within 2026, the count moved by about 7 regions over roughly 6 weeks (June to August).

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no prediction market or Metaculus question on this. None of the markets you collected (Kalshi or Polymarket on the SNB, Swiss referendums, the Jets) is related.
- An NZZ article reports a Copernicus outlook giving a 60-80% chance of above-average precipitation in Switzerland and Germany for November to January. I couldn't verify this because the article is paywalled. [NZZ](https://www.nzz.ch/wissenschaft/duerre-in-der-schweiz-die-pegel-an-zuerichsee-und-bodensee-sinken-so-tief-wie-noch-nie-ld.10025887)

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-11-05 onward: weekly bulletins every Thursday (Nov 5, 12, 19, 26). The map updates roughly weekly, usually on Mondays.
- Early November (roughly the first ten days): dry under high pressure. The bulletin expects soil moisture deficits to grow in all regions while it stays dry. [Bulletin](https://www.trockenheit.admin.ch/de/trockenheit/trockenheitsbulletin)
- Mid to late November: more frequent rain from the west, about normal north of the Alps and below normal south of them. The 30- and 90-day deficits are expected to stay about the same, and low river flows are likely to come back.
- In cold spells, precipitation falls as snow at altitude, so it may not count toward easing the drought right away.

I don't know yet what the platform will show on December 1, but right now it lists zero of its 38 regions as "Extremely dry". That is below the question's 1.5 to 25.5 range. I got this from the platform's own geodata service, which feeds the map, for the week of October 26 to November 1, 2026.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-02: The platform page was "Updated on 11/02/2026" for the situation up to 11/01/2026. Its headline says the drought is continuing ("Die Trockenheitssituation hält an"). The page text gives no counts per class, only a map and a five-level legend. [trockenheit.admin.ch](https://www.trockenheit.admin.ch/en)
- 2026-11-04: I pulled each region's level from the geo.admin service behind the map. All 38 regions came back, valid from 26.10.2026 to 01.11.2026. [geo.admin API](https://api3.geo.admin.ch/rest/services/api/MapServer/find?layer=ch.bafu.trockenheitsindex&searchText=1&searchField=id&returnGeometry=false&contains=true)
  - **Extremely dry: 0**
  - **Very dry: 18.** Bernese Plateau, Oberaargau, Upper Emmental, Freiamt, Western Central Switzerland, Eastern Bernese Oberland, Eastern Swiss Plateau, Lake Zurich Region, Eastern Central Switzerland, Uri Alps, Surselva, Glarus Alps, North-Central Grisons, South-Central Grisons, Rhine Valley, Prättigau, Visp valleys, Goms.
  - **Dry: 6**
  - **Slightly dry: 13.** These are mostly the Jura, western Switzerland and Ticino.
  - **Not dry: 1** (Sottoceneri).
- How the index works: each region's level is the second-highest of several measures (30, 90 and 730-day rain, soil moisture, river flow), ranked against 1991-2020. It is recalculated daily, and the team reviews it weekly. [drought index](https://www.trockenheit.admin.ch/en/drought/drought-index)
- The raw data files were updated 2026-11-04 18:00 UTC. They are zip files I could not open. [STAC](https://data.geo.admin.ch/api/stac/v0.9/collections/ch.bafu.trockenheitsdaten-numerisch/items)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. The current value is 0, and 18 regions sit one level below "Extremely dry", so a renewed dry spell could push several of them up.
- One search summary of a 2 November report mentioned extreme drought around Lake Zurich, the Glarus Alps and the Rhine valley. That conflicts with the API, which rates all three "Very dry" for the week to November 1. I could not find or check that report.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-04: MeteoNews expects little rain in the north and east over the weekend of 7 and 8 November. [MeteoNews via meteo-ch](https://meteo-ch.ch/de/previsions-15-jours/alle.html)
- 2026-11-02: Graubünden says most of its river basins hit historic lows this summer, and about 5,000 fish were moved. [swissinfo](https://www.swissinfo.ch/eng/emissions-reduction/gr-around-5000-fish-have-been-relocated-due-to-the-drought/92314947)
- 2026-10-29: The weekly federal bulletin (next one due 5 November) said:
  - Recent rain eased the drought locally, but the overall situation is still tense.
  - The 90-day rain deficit is moderate to large almost everywhere. It is worst in the Uri and Glarus Alps, Surselva and northern Grisons, at 50-70% below normal.
  - Soil moisture deficits on the northern Alpine slopes and the Plateau are still considerable to extreme.
  - Outlook: dry under high pressure for the first ten days of November, then more frequent westerly rain, roughly normal north of the Alps and below normal in the south. Deficits are expected to persist, and soil deficits would worsen without rain.
  
  [bulletin](https://www.trockenheit.admin.ch/en/drought/drought-bulletin)
- Late October 2026: MeteoNews says October's rain deficit shrank from about 29% to 8%, but lakes and groundwater stay at record lows. [MeteoNews](https://meteonews.ch/en/News/N16931/October-was-too-mild_-slightly-too-dry_-and-too-cloudy)
- 2026-10-12: Over the previous 30 days, rain was under 50% of normal. [swissinfo](https://www.swissinfo.ch/eng/climate-adaptation/the-rain-brought-only-a-temporary-respite/92201760)
- Early November 2026: A Meteo News meteorologist expects "hardly anything" in the first ten days of November. [Tages-Anzeiger](https://www.tagesanzeiger.ch/wetter-schweiz-kommt-im-november-endlich-regen-966057637491)

## 4. Base rates
- Summer 2026 peak, article undated but probably July or August: the environment office rated 20 of 38 regions extremely dry, 13 very dry, 2 dry and 3 slightly dry. [Blick](https://www.blick.ch/sonntagsblick/wegen-anhaltender-trockenheit-geht-uns-das-trinkwasser-aus-id22151220.html)
- 2026-07-10: MeteoSwiss had a level 4 drought warning for all of Switzerland except parts of Ticino and Graubünden. [iamexpat](https://www.iamexpat.ch/expat-info/swiss-news/drought-warning-switzerland)
- Trend: the count fell from about 20 in summer to 0 by late October, after the October rains.
- The platform only launched in 2025, so I found no long history of how weekly counts move. The 2nd-percentile threshold for "Extremely dry" makes it a rare class outside major droughts.
- The index weighs 730-day rain and river flow, so long-term deficits can hold levels up. But any region now needs to rise a full level to count.
- I could not find week-by-week counts for September and October.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no prediction market or expert forecast on this question. All the listed Kalshi and Polymarket markets are unrelated: Swiss central bank rates, referendums, the Federal Council election, the NY Jets.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Weekly bulletins on Thursdays: 5, 12, 19 and 26 November. The map's validity week moves forward each week.
- Weather: dry until about 10 November, then the westerly regime the bulletin forecasts. Uncertain talk of a wet, mild El Niño winter. [bote.ch](https://www.bote.ch/nachrichten/schweizundwelt/wetter-schweiz-winter-wird-wohl-nass-und-mild-art-1729932)
- The platform's map service also has 1 to 3 week forecasts of the index (time steps 2 to 4), but only as images, so I could not read them. [retrieve data](https://www.trockenheit.admin.ch/en/further-information/retrieve-data)
- St. Gallen's next canton update is due no earlier than 16 November. [sg.ch](https://www.sg.ch/umwelt-natur/wasser/trockenheit.html)

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) About 4 weeks remain. Resolution is based on the platform's state around December 1, 2026, which will most likely reflect the update of roughly November 30 (situation to about November 29).

(b) No per-region count is available for November. The last hard counts are 13 of 38 extremely dry on June 23 and 20 of 38 on about August 2. In late September, "nearly all" regions were reported at the top level, probably 25 to 33. The November 2 update says the situation "remains tense," with temporary easing in some regions.

(c) If nothing changed, my estimate of the current count is roughly 14 to 24. October rain probably moved the West, Northwest, Jura and possibly parts of the Mittelland out of the top class. The central and eastern Alps, Graubünden, Valais and the southern Alps probably remain extremely dry.

(d) If the trend continued, the count would keep falling slowly. The first ten days of November are dry and deficits will grow. After that, near-normal rain is expected north of the Alps and below-normal rain to the south, with 30- and 90-day deficits roughly stable. Lakes and groundwater are near record lows, which keeps longer-timescale indicators extreme. A slow decline points to about 10 to 18 by December 1.

(e) Historical variation: the count moved by about 7 regions in 6 weeks during summer, and probably by 10 or more from late September to early November. Over 4 weeks, a swing of 5 to 10 regions is plausible.

(f) Expectations of experts and markets: there are no markets. The bulletin expects deficits to persist and SRF says several months of above-average rain are needed. The unverified Copernicus outlook (60-80% chance of above-average precipitation for November to January) favors easing. The question creator's range of 2 to 25 is consistent with my central estimate.

(g) Unexpected scenarios:
- Low: a wet, mild, westerly pattern in mid to late November delivers well-above-normal rain across the north and the Alps. Only a few southern or inner-Alpine regions stay extremely dry, leaving 0 to 3.
- High: persistent high pressure through November, with precipitation falling as snow at altitude, pushes soil moisture and runoff deficits back to extreme almost everywhere. That would give 26 to 32 regions, similar to September.

(b) **Latest known value:** The latest exact count is from about August 2, 2026: 20 of 38 regions were "Extremely dry." In late September, "nearly all" regions were reported at the top level, probably more than 25. There is no exact count for October or November. The November 2 platform headline says the situation "remains tense," with only temporary easing in some regions.

(c) **If nothing changed:** The current count is unknown. My best guess is that October rain pulled the West, Northwest and Jura below "Extremely dry." The central and eastern Alps, northern Graubünden, Valais, and parts of the northern Alpine side and Mittelland probably remain extremely dry. That suggests roughly 12 to 20 regions now.

(d) **If the trend continued:**
- Early November is dry, so deficits will grow.
- Mid to late November is expected to bring near-normal rain north of the Alps and below-normal rain to the south.
- Near-normal rain does not erase 90-day deficits, and lakes and groundwater are at record lows.
- Some easing is likely north of the Alps, while the south and the Alps stay dry.
- Net effect: a modest decline, to somewhere around 10 to 15.

(e) **Historical variation:** From June to August the count moved by about 7 regions in 6 weeks. From August to September it rose by perhaps 10 or more, then fell after October rain. Over 4 weeks a swing of plus or minus 8 to 10 is plausible. The platform launched in 2025, so there is little history to go on.

(f) **Experts and markets:**
- No market covers this question.
- The drought bulletin expects deficits to stay roughly unchanged through November.
- An unverified Copernicus seasonal outlook favors above-average precipitation from November to January.
- The question creator's range is 2 to 25.

(g) **Unexpected scenarios:**
- **Low outcome:** A wet, mild late November with repeated Atlantic fronts gives large surpluses north of the Alps, and the index responds quickly. Only a few Alpine or southern regions stay extremely dry, giving 0 to 3.
- **High outcome:** Persistent high pressure all of November, with fog on the Plateau and no rain, drives record-low flows. Nearly all regions return to "Extremely dry," giving 28 to 33.
